$comment: OBRS-602. The declared partition of the Playwright suite. Enforced by scripts/check-e2e-lanes.mjs; explained in docs/e2e-lanes.md. A spec belongs to exactly one lane, and the lane says what the spec needs to be TRUE, not what it happens to run under today.

lanes.GATE: Hermetic. Intercepts every call it makes, so it needs no backend, no seeded data and no external service. This is the only lane that is a merge gate. Run: npm run e2e:gate
lanes.GATE-BLOCKED: Mocks all of its own API traffic but still boots with a session minted from live SIT by e2e/global-setup.ts -- as fragile as SIT despite needing nothing from it. EMPTY since OBRS-618 moved all four members into GATE via e2e/support/gate-admin-session.ts, and that is the intended steady state: a spec parked here should leave again, not settle.
lanes.SIT-LIVE: Deliberately hits the deployed SIT backend, per docs/adr/0001-admin-e2e-hits-real-sit-backend.md -- mocking would defeat the point, which is catching contract drift. Not a gate: shared mutable environment.
lanes.OWN-DB: Needs booking/report states that can only exist by construction, so it provisions its own database. See playwright.local.config.ts for the reasoning. Never runnable against SIT.
lanes.CAPTURE: Not a test. A screenshot/evidence script kept for reproducing card artefacts. Asserts little and is not expected to pass unattended.

specs.why: Fulfils every /api/** call from its own fixture and seeds NO session at all -- signed-out is the assertion, not a shortcut, since the whole card is about a customer with no account. Proves what neither end can: that the navbar link on / actually resolves to the page, and that the phone number rides in the POST body rather than the URL.

Fulfils every /api/** call from its own fixture and seeds no session at all. Measures the station bar's geometry at this lane's pinned 1280px viewport -- the ROW layout the three Karma specs cannot reach, because their window is 800px and the 992px stack switch is a viewport query.

Fulfils every /api/** call from its own fixture and makes /api/stops fail on purpose (route.abort, i.e. the same status 0 the OBRS-642 timeout raises); seeds no session. Proves the claim no component spec can: that NO SweetAlert2 modal reaches the page, which the HTTP interceptor raises into document.body outside every Karma fixture. The two populations are the two tests -- localStorage roster seeded (silent) versus cleared (inline message plus retry).

Screenshots only, no assertions -- and that is the requirement, not a shortcut: it has to run unchanged against BOTH the pre-card and post-card runtimes so the BEFORE image is the real previous behaviour rather than a reconstruction. Stage comes from OBRS_CAPTURE_STAGE; the BEFORE pass is taken with `git stash push -- src/` applied while ng serve rebuilds. Every assertion for this card lives in obrs-1222-station-load-error.spec.ts on the GATE lane.
Single catch-all page.route on **/api/** fulfils every path; fake token seeded into localStorage. Nothing reaches the network.
Stubs its public calls and ABORTS unstubbed **/api/private/** traffic, failing by name if a call escapes (OBRS-535). Fake token, no real session.
Anonymous, fixture-driven. Became hermetic in OBRS-602 once GET /api/routes -- the call that resolves the slug for its own pickup-dropoff mock -- was stubbed too.
Anonymous; stubs stops, schedules and pickup-dropoff per describe. OBRS-602 added the GET /api/routes stub it had always left live.

Booking path on fixture stations and schedules. OBRS-602 added the GET /api/routes stub that /home's route-map issues. OBRS-856 split it in two: the walk is anonymous only as far as the review page (still open to guests on purpose), after which one test seeds a customer session in localStorage and the other asserts the guest is sent to /login. Still hermetic -- the seeded token is never validated by anything, since every API call is intercepted.

OBRS-854. Walks the counter-QR path end to end at a 390px phone viewport: logged out at /account, bounced through AuthGuard to /login, back to /account, dialog opened, translated confirm phrase typed, and DELETE /api/private/users/me asserted off the wire rather than by a success toast. Hermetic by construction -- it mints no session at all (arriving logged OUT is the scenario under test), one page.route fulfils every /api/** call including the login it performs, and accounts.google.com is aborted so /login's GIS script never leaves the box. It also seeds OBRS-867's obrs_analytics_consent_v1 to an ANSWERED value for most cases, because that bar is fixed to the bottom of the viewport and this page puts the close-account card last on purpose; the unanswered overlap is not hidden but pinned by its own test, which asks document.elementFromPoint what is really on top of the button rather than reasoning about z-index.

OBRS-867 AC-1, declared by OBRS-882 -- the card shipped this spec without a lanes.json entry, so it belonged to no lane and ran nowhere but by hand. OWN-DB rather than GATE for the same reason that lane exists: it asserts a state that can only exist by construction. It needs the `analytics-e2e` build configuration, the ONLY one carrying a real measurement ID, because it measures consent on the WIRE -- no request to googletagmanager/clarity/google-analytics before accept, and a MUST-CATCH case proving both really do fire after. Against any other build the IDs are blank, the loader no-ops, and every 'nothing was requested' assertion passes vacuously. It touches no database, but the lane's rule -- provisions the environment its premise needs, never runnable against SIT -- is the one that fits.

OBRS-1195 AC-5. Same lane and same build as obrs-867-analytics-consent-gate.spec.ts, for the same reason -- the `analytics-e2e` configuration is the only one carrying a measurement ID, and on a blank-ID build every count here would be zero and every expectation would pass while proving nothing. What it adds is the layer further out: the 867/874 suites count requests for the TAG, this one counts the `page_view` hits the tag then sends to /g/collect. That distinction is the card: `sendEvent` was being called and the wire was silent, and between them sit `suspended`, `ga-disable-<id>`, gtag's queue and `send_page_view: false`. Its first case is a CONTROL, not a courtesy -- 'exactly one page_view' is an absence claim about the second one, which a broken parser and a healthy app report identically. AC-3 (accepting on a staff route sends nothing) is NOT here on purpose: the consent banner is hidden on a restricted route, so no browser can click it; that arm is pinned in analytics.service.spec.ts, and the negative arm a browser CAN prove -- declining sends nothing at all -- is here instead.

OBRS-631. The 2.0 privacy notice as rendered, plus the AFTER picture the card needs as evidence. CAPTURE only because of the screenshot -- the four assertions beside it are load-bearing and can each fail for a real reason. They cover the half scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs structurally cannot see: the notice arrives through [innerHTML], and a
    inside a

    (what 2.0 would have been without the template change to a div) is closed early by the parser, so the markup collapses while every string gate reading the JSON stays green. Hence counting the h2 elements AND asserting they are direct children of .policy-body. Needs no backend, no seed and no third party -- the page renders from public/i18n/*.json and privacy-policy.version.ts alone -- so it runs against the plain development build on its own port.

OBRS-874 AC-5. Reads document.cookie / localStorage / sessionStorage before and after accepting on the DEPLOYED SIT site and prints the DIFFERENCE -- the list OBRS-631 AC-5 copies into the notice's cookie section. SIT-LIVE and never a gate: it consents to real GA4 and Clarity tags on a real deployment, which is precisely what makes the answer true; the analytics-e2e build's IDs are invalid on purpose, so its tags 404 and store nothing, and measuring there would produce an empty list that reads like an answer. It asserts a difference rather than a pinned list, because a hardcoded list would have to be edited to stay green -- turning a vendor adding a cookie from a signal into a chore. Two must-catches keep it honest in both directions: no vendor-shaped name may exist BEFORE consent (that would mean the gate is broken), and at least one must appear AFTER (otherwise the empty census is a false statement waiting to be published).

OBRS-874 AC-2. Same premise and therefore the same lane as obrs-867-analytics-consent-gate.spec.ts: it can only be true on the `analytics-e2e` build, the one configuration carrying measurement IDs, because it measures a WITHDRAWAL on the wire. It asserts the two halves separately because different mechanisms guarantee them -- without a reload, collection stops at the vendor (`ga-disable-<id>` plus `clarity('stop')`, driven by AnalyticsService's isGranted$ subscription); after a reload, the scripts are never injected at all because load() is only reached while granted. It reaches the policy page by CLICKING the footer link rather than page.goto, because goto is a fresh document and would throw away the very tags whose in-place shutdown is the claim. Carries its own MUST-CATCH accept leg for the same reason the 867 suite does: on a blank-ID build every 'nothing was requested' expectation passes while proving nothing. Touches no database; OWN-DB is the lane for 'provisions the environment its premise needs, never runnable against SIT'.

OBRS-1141 BEFORE/AFTER evidence for the announced-delay disclosure on search results. Hermetic on the gate lane's terms (it reuses e2e/support/customer-pages.ts, which fulfils every /api/** call and aborts Maps), but its purpose is the pictures in the card, so CAPTURE. Like obrs-867-capture it is a harder-working capture than most: the on-time row must carry NO disclosure (AC2) and the badge's contrast is MEASURED off the painted pixels in BOTH themes, which is the only way to know the component rule outranked `body.is-dark .schedule-item * { color: !important }` (OBRS-767).

OBRS-867 AFTER evidence, declared by OBRS-882 (shipped undeclared alongside the spec above). Screenshots of the consent bar from the same build whose network behaviour the AC-1 suite asserts, plus a MEASURED contrast pair read off the painted pixels rather than out of variables.scss. Its purpose is a picture, so CAPTURE -- but note it is a harder-working capture than most in this lane: the contrast assertion can fail for a real reason.

OBRS-882. Two stubbed home-page calls (stops, schedules search) and nothing else, so it needs no backend by construction. It exists as the counterpart to e2e/support/analytics-consent.ts: with a settled PDPA answer now seeded lane-wide, this is the ONLY spec that still loads a page with OBRS-867's consent bar UP, and without it the seeding would be a mute rather than a repair. Asks document.elementFromPoint what is really on top of the usability FAB rather than reasoning about z-index -- the overlap is deliberate per the component's own SCSS, so it is pinned, not overturned. obrs-854-account-deeplink.spec.ts asks the same question of a different button at a phone viewport.

OBRS-1372 BEFORE/AFTER evidence. Screenshots only, no assertions -- and that is the requirement, not a shortcut: it has to run unchanged against BOTH runtimes so the BEFORE frame is the real previous behaviour. Shoots four customer pages at the iPhone 14's 390x664 scrolled as far down as the document allows, which is the defect in one frame. Stage comes from OBRS_CAPTURE_STAGE; the BEFORE pass is taken with `git stash push -- src/` applied. Every assertion for this card lives in obrs-1372-consent-banner-reachability.spec.ts on the GATE lane.

OBRS-1372. Reuses the contrast gate's customer-page fixtures (every /api/** call stubbed, Maps aborted), so it needs nothing but a browser. The spec above pins the bar's overlap with the FAB as deliberate; this one asks the question that overlap does not answer -- with the bar `position: fixed; bottom: 0` and no room reserved for it, the last 246px of every customer page could not be scrolled clear at all, measured on prod at an iPhone 14 viewport. Sweeps all of CUSTOMER_PAGES at 390x664 in Thai (the tall wrap is the defect's precondition) and asks document.elementFromPoint at each control's BEST reachable offset. Deliberately seeds no consent decision -- findUnreachable throws if the bar is absent, so a spec that measured the answered state cannot pass quietly. Carries its own must-catch/must-not-catch fixture first.

Every endpoint it touches is fulfilled from inline constants. OBRS-618 replaced its SIT-minted storageState with a synthetic in-browser session (e2e/support/gate-admin-session.ts); it now passes against no backend at all.

23 routes / 28 fulfils cover the backend entirely, and one test reads i18n JSON off disk -- no network. OBRS-618 swapped the SIT-minted storageState for the synthetic session and added an afterEach that fails by name if any authenticated call escapes its stubs.
Fully stubbed walk-in schedules and segments; the SIT-minted storageState was the only thing keeping it out, and OBRS-618 removed that dependency.

56 fulfilling routes. Its comment blamed a fake token for changing behaviour; OBRS-618 checked the code and nothing in src/app decodes a JWT -- AuthService treats it as an opaque string and reads roles from a separate localStorage key. The real cause was the OBRS-535 one: an unmocked authenticated call 401s and force-logs-out, which cannot happen in a lane with no backend. Promoted only after all 42 cases passed here.

OBRS-584. Sweeps eight customer pages in both themes and scores WCAG 1.4.3 (text) and 1.4.11 (control boundary) from getComputedStyle. Hermetic by construction: one page.route fulfils every /api/** call from inline fixtures, Maps is aborted, the session is a synthetic localStorage token and the booking flow is reached by dispatching the app's own NgRx actions rather than by driving the funnel. It needs a DEVELOPMENT build (window.ng, for the store seed), which is exactly what this lane's webServer serves.

OBRS-753. Asserts no component host in the review module is display:inline while wrapping block-level children, that a click at the confirm button's centre still hits the button, and that the fix moved no geometry at any of the four media-query widths. Hermetic on the same terms as customer-contrast-gate, whose fixtures and NgRx store seed it reuses (e2e/support/customer-pages.ts): no backend, no session minted anywhere, Maps aborted.

OBRS-767. Removes every dark-theme.scss declaration from the live CSSOM in turn and fails if nothing on the page changed. A rule that parses, matches its element and still loses to Angular's [_ngcontent] specificity is invisible to any source-reading check, and that shape had hidden the entire dark footer at 2.40:1 for the life of the feature. Reuses customer-pages.ts, so it is hermetic on exactly the same terms as the contrast gate, plus /register and /how-to-book to reach dark-theme.scss sections 5 and 9.

OBRS-775. Widens OBRS-753's one-module check to every page this lane can reach hermetically -- nine customer pages, nine public/auth-entry routes, twenty-nine admin/staff/session-bound routes, 47 screens in all -- and fails on any display:inline custom-element host holding in-flow block children that is not named on its ALLOW list with a reason. OBRS-776 added the twelve admin/staff pages and a second half: it derives from the source tree which components render p-tabview/p-tabpanel/p-card/p-calendar and fails on any the sweep did not MOUNT, because a clean census cannot tell a page that is well-formed from a page nobody opened -- which is what a global rule in src/styles/ needs before it can be trusted. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane: it reuses e2e/support/customer-pages.ts for the customer group and stubs every /api/** call itself for the other two, aborts Maps, and mints no session anywhere. Needs a DEVELOPMENT build for the same reason customer-contrast-gate does (window.ng, for the NgRx store seed). OBRS-782 reached the last seven components OBRS-776 had excused by variant, by giving SweepPage a `fixture` (per-screen JSON answered ahead of the empty backend) alongside its `act`: NOT_SWEPT is down to app-parcel-trip-form, which expires by itself when its feature flag flips. Still hermetic -- a fixture is one more canned answer from the same page.route, not a backend. The five added screens turned up three malformed hosts nothing had ever measured.

The spec ADR-0001 was written for: create Vehicle / ScheduleSet / Schedules against the real backend so a malformed payload cannot pass. OBRS-617 added e2e/support/sit-sweep.ts, called in beforeAll (self-heal) and afterAll (leave zero) -- it no longer leaves TEST- litter behind on SIT.

OBRS-617 AC-4. Purely API-driven: seeds a TEST- route + ScheduleSet on the real backend, runs sweepSitTestLitter(), and asserts both are gone. MUST use its own config -- it has no page.goto, so it needs no webServer/globalSetup, and riding playwright.config.ts would drag the ng-serve build that a fresh worktree cannot compile (OBRS-536). Mutates SIT by design, self-cleaning.
Stubs the users list and the unlock PUT because SIT pre-dates the locked field, but the rest of the admin shell is served live.
Queries the SIT API directly and asserts the six seeded dropoff stops still carry placehold.co URLs -- by design it goes red when the Places backfill succeeds.
Zero mocks. Posts a real verify-email request and performs a real login, with a 60s allowance for Koyeb cold start.
Zero mocks and a real admin session across /staff and /admin shells; pure live-render coverage.
Deliberately leaves /api/routes* live and asserts the seeded SIT stop lists (19 pickup, first 'Nong chak') -- verified still accurate on 2026-07-21.
MUST use its own config: the defect is a CSS rule below 576px and the assertions are meaningless at the default 1280px, where it would pass while measuring nothing.
Needs five E2E-* bookings including already-rescheduled, cancelled and seat-collision states, and mutates them. On SIT those states can only be produced by running the spec, which spends them.

OBRS-732. Needs a booking that is `pending`, unexpired, unpaid and free of any in-flight payment -- five conditions PaymentService.validateBookingForPayment enforces and which the reschedule fixture deliberately does not satisfy (its design keeps `payments` out of it entirely). Provisions its own database through the OBRS-184 boot script with E2E_FIXTURE_SQL pointed at obrs-732-3ds-fixture.sql. NOT hermetic on purpose: it really charges api.omise.co in TEST mode and really walks Omise's hosted 3DS page, because 3-D Secure leaves our origin and returns through return_uri -- a mocked one would evidence nothing. Never a gate: it depends on a third party's uptime. (OBRS-735: this used to also cite an Actions minute ceiling -- false, this repo is PUBLIC and unmetered.) SCOPE BOUNDARY: it stops at /payment/result with a real chrg_ id, and deliberately does NOT assert fully_paid -- after 3DS the charge stays pending until OmiseWebhookService receives an INBOUND call from Omise, which cannot reach a laptop, and nothing else in the system reconciles it (the result page only polls, the endpoint only reads the database, no @Scheduled job covers it). Asserting settlement here would be permanently red and would read as a product defect.
Needs booking OBRS483-OPEN with a null seat from its SQL fixture, and a backend built from the OBRS-483 branch. The frontend alone is not sufficient.

OBRS-766. Every case here CONSUMES the booking it acts on -- cancelling is the thing under test -- so each seeds its own walk-in sale through the real API instead of depending on a booking a previous run already spent. Needs states SIT cannot be asked for: a CASH sale (to reach the OBRS-669 second-person step-up), a payment-less booking (to resolve MANUAL_REFUND_REQUIRED), and a booking departing inside the 2h window (produced by rewriting booking_schedules.departure_date_time, since the seeded cluster starts December 2026). Its globalSetup frees seat inventory first: one pass consumes 7+ of the 14 seats per vehicle type, and without the reset the third pass fails at seeding with BOOKING_ERROR_SEATS_INSUFFICIENT -- which reads exactly like a product regression and is not one. Never a gate: it mutates its own database and shells out to psql.

OBRS-766. The card's load-bearing case in one continuous flow: a SALESPERSON logs in, finds a walk-in booking they did NOT sell, sees the refund preview before committing, and cancels it under the second-person cash approval -- the proof that act-on-behalf (OBRS-661) and the cash step-up (OBRS-669) are reachable at all, since neither had a UI before this card. Shares the OWN-DB reasoning and globalSetup above. Also asserts the masked phone never appears raw in the DOM or in any response body, so it doubles as the anti-enumeration guard for GET /api/private/bookings/search.

OBRS-577. Every claim on this card -- first page is exactly 20, Load more APPENDS rather than replaces, the count line names the FILTERED total, the button hides itself on the last page, and a mutation reload keeps the whole loaded window instead of collapsing back to 20 -- needs one account holding well over 20 bookings in two independently-sized status buckets. No SIT seed account clears 20 (customer@system.local was MEASURED at 37 during this card's live run and used read-only as the baseline), and manufacturing dozens of bookings on shared SIT is not a reasonable ask, so the lane owns its database: obrs577qa, rebuilt every run from schema.sql -> data.sql -> e2e/fixtures/obrs577-load-more-fixture.sql (44 CONFIRMED + 7 CANCELLED = 52 under All). The mutation-reload case is the one that cannot be had any other way: it really cancels one of 40 loaded Confirmed rows and asserts 39, because the two defects that shipped and were caught here -- an effect guard reading a flag its own action's reducer had already set, and a reducer reset zeroing the page window under the effect -- are both invisible to a unit test that stubs state with overrideSelector. Never a gate: it mutates its own database, and its BACKEND port is deliberately :8181, the same one playwright.local.config.ts binds (environment.e2e.ts:26 hardcodes apiUrl and is not build-time-configurable), so the two OWN-DB lanes must run SEQUENTIALLY. Its OBRS_BACKEND_DIR is a throwaway detached backend worktree; recreate it if absent with `git -C ../OBRS-backend worktree add --detach ../OBRS-backend-wt-577qa origin/dev` -- pointing it at the shared ../OBRS-backend clone would build whatever branch that clone happens to be parked on.
Asserts exactly four seeded reports and a QA-SEED follow-up, then edits them irreversibly. Requires a fresh obrs433qa database.

specs.config: none -- run by hand against obrs564qa on :8080
specs.why: Calls http://localhost:8080 directly and writes the global booking cap to 45, resetting it in a separate test that a mid-suite failure skips. Must never point at a shared environment.

specs.config: none -- run by hand against obrs576qa on :8080
specs.why: Asserts hand-seeded synthetic history rows that no script in this repo creates, and appends new rows on every run. Provisions nothing itself.

specs.config: none -- no committed config runs it. It is hermetic and uses baseURL-relative navigation, so it needs only a `testMatch` pointing at it; run it with `npx playwright test --config=playwright.gate.config.ts` ONLY after temporarily adding it, which the lane gate will then reject. Adding it to the GATE lane for real is the clean fix if the capture is still wanted.
specs.why: Fully mocked and technically hermetic, but its purpose is producing the OBRS-296 before/after e-ticket screenshots, not asserting behaviour.
Screenshot script. Expects two servers started by hand on :4575 and :4576 -- one of them serving origin/dev for the BEFORE shot.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-702 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4702 and :4703 -- :4702 serving a throwaway worktree at origin/dev 3eff9dc1 for the BEFORE shot. Hermetic otherwise (synthetic session, stubbed config reads), but its purpose is evidence, not a verdict.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-391 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4391 and :4392 -- :4391 serving the main clone at origin/dev for the BEFORE shot. NOT hermetic on purpose: it stubs every /api/** call but reaches cdn.omise.co for real, because the claim being evidenced is that the card fields now render in a third-party iframe and a stubbed frame would prove nothing. environment.base.ts carries a test-mode publishable key, so no charge is possible.

OBRS-775's AC3 evidence, re-used by OBRS-776: the border box of EVERY element on all 39 pages of the host-box sweep (27 when OBRS-775 wrote this), at the four media-query widths, captured once with the `:host { display }` additions absent (OBRS775_PHASE=before) and once with them applied. The AFTER phase reads the baseline back and fails on any box that moved more than 0.5px, so it is an assertion rather than a screenshot -- but it is still a two-run, run-by-hand comparison, which is why it is not in GATE. Hermetic: it reuses the same e2e/support/host-boxes.ts fixtures the gate spec does, so no backend and no database.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-742 before/after. The ONLY capture here that needs a live stack: it logs into a real backend on :8080 over a disposable obrs742qa database and photographs six history rows written through OBRS-730's real owner-override endpoint, because the INSERT row (old_value NULL) this card fixes cannot be produced any other way -- OBRS-722's capture had to stub its rows precisely because that endpoint did not exist yet. BEFORE and AFTER are served one at a time on :4200, the dev profile's only allowed CORS origin, BEFORE from a throwaway detached worktree at origin/dev 1b5c852d. Evidence, not a verdict.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-722 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4722 and :4723 -- :4722 serving a throwaway detached worktree at the then-current origin/dev (45c66cbd) for the BEFORE shot. Hermetic otherwise (synthetic session, one stubbed history page), but its purpose is evidence, not a verdict.
Hardcodes http://localhost:4575 for every navigation, bypassing baseURL, and depends on recent-route history existing for the seeded customer.

OBRS-769's evidence: every sighting of the two muted text tokens with the background it MEASURED under, on the contrast gate's own eight pages in both themes. The gate prints only what fails, and this card turned on what still PASSED -- #989ba4 was 2.78:1 on white at 39 sightings and 5.38:1 on the dark booking card at one, so a single repoint could not serve both. Hermetic (it reuses customer-pages.ts fixtures and MEASURE, so no backend), and it does assert its own population is non-empty, but its output is a census for a human to read rather than a verdict. Re-run it before changing $text-lightblack: npx playwright test --config=playwright.obrs769.config.ts

OBRS-769 before/after evidence. Two servers started by hand -- :4761 a throwaway detached worktree at origin/dev c1388c27 for the BEFORE shot, :4762 this one -- and run once per phase with OBRS769_PHASE. TWO separate clipped frames per phase rather than one composed sheet, because OBRS-811 composed four dropdown panels into a single image and a reviewer read it as a layout bug. Hermetic otherwise (customer-pages.ts fixtures), but its purpose is a picture, not a verdict.

OBRS-907. Seeds a synthetic admin session (seedGateAdminSession, no live SIT/storageState) and hangs the one call it depends on -- GET .../private/notifications never resolves, via a route handler registered after the shell's own stub so it wins by Playwright's reverse-registration-order matching -- so NotificationInboxService.loading$ stays true and the notification-bell's first-load spinner never races to the empty state. Asserts prefers-reduced-motion via page.emulateMedia against the real compiled admin-theme.scss + loading-state.component.scss cascade, with a positive control (asserts the un-reduced case actually rotates first) before trusting the frozen-but-visible assertion.

OBRS-939. Asserts that the admin shell still ANSWERS -- a trivial page.evaluate must resolve within 5s, sampled 5s after navigation because the freeze started 2.6-3.8s in and a check that samples immediately passes while broken. It caught a change-detection loop that no unit test could reach (Karma runs one detectChanges() by hand; the loop needs a real zone driving ticks) and that no screenshot could show (the last paint before the freeze stays on screen). Population is the shell, not the page the bug was reported on: /admin/dashboard under abort, 500 and 401, plus all five OBRS-151..155 analytics pages. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane -- synthetic in-browser session, every /api/private/** call answered by the spec itself, no backend.

OBRS-813. The cancel modal now names the reschedule door, and the card's hard limit is that this costs the traveler no extra click on the way OUT. That is measured with a control arm rather than a constant: the same cancel journey is walked on a reschedule-ELIGIBLE booking (offer rendered) and on an ineligible one (the pre-card layout), in one run, and the two click counts are compared -- a hardcoded number would be one nobody measured before the change. Also pins the two things the offer must never do: cancel anything by itself, and appear on a booking the backend would refuse to reschedule. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane -- synthetic customer session in localStorage, every /api/** call fulfilled by the spec, no backend.

OBRS-942. The sibling of obrs-813 on the lane 813 never reached: a card/gateway payment, whose cancel used to be a plain SweetAlert that never mentioned reschedule. Walks that journey on a reschedule-ELIGIBLE booking and on an ineligible one and compares click counts against the manual lane, for the same reason 813 does -- the number that matters is the one nobody had measured before the change. Two assertions cannot be made any other way: the cancel request body is read off the wire with request.postDataJSON() and must be exactly {}, because the FE now passes {refundDestination: undefined} and only JSON.stringify dropping undefined keys keeps that byte-identical to the old call; and dismissing the modal must leave Cancel ENABLED on the same booking AND on a different one, which is where the reducer left cancellingBookingId set and disabled Cancel app-wide until reload -- invisible to 4557 unit tests. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane -- synthetic customer session in localStorage, every /api/** call fulfilled by the spec, no backend.

OBRS-627. /refund-policy is linked from every page's footer and from /payment, so a customer reads it before paying, and until this card it described a refund the system has never performed -- original paper ticket, ID copies, in-person cash pickup, forfeiture after 7 days -- while naming no refund rate at all. The rates now render from GET /api/cancellation-policy. Three things live only in the assembled app and are why this needs a browser rather than more unit tests: whether the shipped page calls that endpoint at all, whether a raw {{refundRateEarlyPercent}} can reach a customer, and whether the retired clauses are gone from the REAL public/i18n/th.json rather than from a TestBed fixture -- all three are what went wrong on the identical claim one page over (OBRS-564). The wire values are 36h/3h/90%/45%, deliberately not the shipped 24/2/80/50, so 'rendered from the wire' cannot be confused with 'rendered from a literal'. Also pins AC-3: a failed config read shows an inline error and states NO rate, never a hardcoded fallback. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane -- every /api/** call fulfilled by the spec, no backend, no session.

OBRS-1207. Replaces the two FAB-overlap cases in report-usability-issue.spec.ts, which compared the `position: fixed` FAB's viewport box against `.select-btn`'s and never pinned the scroll -- so the verdict was a function of where the page came to rest, not of the code. Proven, not argued: the byte-identical tree 098022f8 passed on PR #167, went red on the dev merge 8c43dcec, and passed 6/6 locally, having been green for months while the defect was present. This spec SOLVES for the scroll offsets at which an element's click point falls inside the FAB band -- a closed interval per element, so no offset can slip between samples -- then scrolls there and asks document.elementFromPoint(), the only oracle that accounts for z-index, stacking contexts, pointer-events and transforms at once. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane: it reuses report-usability-issue's stations/schedules fixtures and stubs every /api/** call it makes.

OBRS-1224. The claim is a DISTANCE in px between the box the customer types a station into and the field they clicked, with the panel flipped upward by Popper -- so it needs a real layout engine, a real 60vh and a real viewport height, none of which Karma has (its window is 800px and fixed, and the three component specs that measure this bar therefore never take the flipped branch). Measured on prod before the fix: 496 px at 1440x900 and 556 px at 1907x1000, against a 48 px field. The spec asserts the AC threshold (no further than one field-height), that the distance is 0 because the typing box IS the field, and that there is exactly ONE typeable box in the group -- a fix that filtered correctly from a second box in the panel would be the bug wearing the fix's clothes. It also asserts data-popper-placement still starts with 'top', because option C on the card was 'stop the panel flipping' and was rejected; without that line a build taking the forbidden route would pass everything else here. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane: it reuses mockPublicPageApis and then sharpens the stop list to 24, because the shared fixture's 2 stops never overflow 60vh, never flip, and would measure the one geometry that was never broken.

OBRS-1370. The lane's own hermeticity, asserted rather than declared. Rule 2 of playwright.gate.config.ts argued this lane was provably hermetic because an unintercepted request hits a dead localhost:8080 -- true only of traffic that travels through `apiUrl`. An absolute third-party URL inside a stylesheet or a fixture never goes near it, so the lane was measured reaching five external hosts on an ordinary sweep (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, accounts.google.com, ssl.gstatic.com, and placehold.co from two specs' fixtures), and a transient gstatic 404 on one of them turned the dev merge red on a tree that had just passed on the PR (OBRS-1369). This spec sweeps the customer pages and fails naming any host outside this machine, with an allow list that costs a sentence per entry. Hermetic by definition: it is the thing that measures it.

OBRS-1308 QA. Its premise can be neither mocked nor borrowed: an owner proposes text, a DIFFERENT person approves it, and only then does the live message change -- so it needs a real backend, a real notification_message_override table, and two seeded accounts whose roles the approval gate actually distinguishes. Against SIT it would be destructive twice over, because an APPROVED override is platform-wide (the table has no owner_id) and the messages it rewrites are SMS, which cannot be recalled once sent; the local stack points the provider at a capture server so nothing leaves the machine. The AC2 arm is why this is kept rather than deleted after the run: it detects the SILENT failure -- API refuses the save, screen shows nothing -- by counting visible error elements after a refused submit, which is exactly the shape that shipped past two green suites.

OBRS-1308 card evidence: the settings tab strip, the owner edit screen with a live {n} violation, the admin inbox and review diff, the post-approval result, and the SMS credit counter showing a raised count with Save still ENABLED -- that last frame is the AC12 decision photographed, since 'display-only, never a gate' is a claim a picture can actually settle. Also carries the AC2 re-run arm: four violation shapes, one AFTER frame each, with the unmatched brace as the primary evidence because it is the one that used to render nothing at all. The BEFORE tab-strip frame is RECONSTRUCTED by removing the new tab from the DOM rather than building origin/dev, and is labeled as reconstructed in the file, on the card and here -- it is not a live BEFORE render and must not be quoted as one.

OBRS-1331 card evidence: /admin/settings at 1280x720 -- the width the owner reported -- in en/th and light/dark, plus a 1600px pair where the strip does NOT wrap. Two hand-started `ng serve` instances and no backend, the same shape OBRS-702 used for this same page: the strip is built entirely from SYSTEM_SETTINGS_TABS on the frontend, so only the Booking Policy read needs stubbing. Kept rather than deleted after the run, for the next card that adds a tab (OBRS-703, OBRS-705).

OBRS-1298 AC2-AC7 -- /admin/stops moved its edit form into a modal and made the table row clickable. OWN-DB because it MUTATES stop rows it did not create (AC5a saves a text field on a stop that already has a photo, to prove the save does not clobber primaryPhotoUrl; AC5b saves padded whitespace and reads the trimmed value back, which only proves anything if the value came back from the server) and it carries NO e2e/support/sit-sweep.ts teardown -- on the shared SIT database those edits would simply stay. Not GATE: intercepting the save would leave only the modal markup, which stop-form-modal.component.spec.ts already covers in unit-test time, and it dismisses SweetAlert with click({force:true}), which that lane forbids for good reason (OBRS-750). It was authored against SIT and redirected to a hand-started local backend mid-run when SIT login started returning 500 for every seeded account (OBRS-1307); that private database is also what makes the mutating cases safe to keep. Three cases are REAL FINDINGS pinned as-is rather than fixed, all in shared code outside this card scope: focus does not enter the dialog on optimistic open, and the 1200 backdrop physically covers the topbar language switcher (z-index 35-40).

OBRS-1333 -- the owner's maintenance-plan tab on /admin/vehicles. OWN-DB because its premise is a database built for it: the obrs1333qa Postgres created by scripts/new-local-db.ps1 plus a fixture script that plants known odometer histories, plan rows and driver assignments, which is the only way the derived nextDueKm/nextDueDate this spec reads off the screen have knowable values at all. Never runnable against SIT: it creates and deactivates plans and would leave them there, and it carries no sit-sweep teardown. ⚠️ The config does NOT provision that database -- it has no globalSetup and no webServer, it only points baseURL at a stack (backend :8080, ng serve :4200) that the operator started first; the same shape as playwright.obrs1298qa.config.ts, and the reason this spec is not a merge gate. Not GATE for the load-bearing reason: intercepting the API would replace exactly the values under test, since every due-date and lead-distance assertion here is about the browser faithfully showing a number the SERVER derived, and a fixture would make those assertions restate themselves. What it deliberately does NOT re-assert is the backend behaviour itself -- the AC1 two-layer constraint, AC3 whichever-first branch, AC4 auto-update on completion, AC5 recipients, AC6 leadKm derivation, AC7's three fallback tiers and AC8 anti-duplicate were each proved once against the API and DB directly (curl + psql) during the QA run, where they can be measured instead of inferred through a screen. Screenshots for the card come from e2e/capture-obrs-1333-maintenance-plan.mjs, which is a script rather than a spec and so has no lane of its own.

OBRS-1258 AC1-AC5 + AC7-AC9 -- the owner's sales-point picker in user-form-modal, the sell page's default pickup, and the EOD sales-point column. OWN-DB and NEVER runnable against SIT for a reason that is not a preference: SIT does not carry the OBRS-1260 backend contract this whole card depends on (measured 2026-08-16, `git merge-base --is-ancestor e68e48ae origin/sit` = false, origin/sit..origin/dev = 33 commits), so every assertion here would exercise the retired `salesPointStop` shape and pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also MUTATES a seeded salesperson's sales-point set and CREATES a user, with no sit-sweep teardown. Like playwright.obrs1298qa.config.ts and playwright.obrs1333.config.ts, the config does NOT provision anything -- it points at a stack the operator started first (backend :8080 on the obrs1258qa database built from schema.sql + lookups.sql + Flyway v96 + data.sql, ng serve :4200) and reuseExistingServer is unconditional. Not GATE for the load-bearing reason: `defaultPickupStopSlug` is resolved SERVER-side per caller from their active sales point, so intercepting /api/private/route-stops would replace the exact value under test and the assertion would restate its own fixture. Two harness traps are pinned in the file itself, both of which first read as product failures: a bare `.admin-dropdown-*` locator is a strict-mode violation (5 of them on this screen), and the route-group header in the trip browser is a COLLAPSE TOGGLE, so clicking it hides the trip you are about to select.
